# Time zone

The system's time zone rules, read through [`GetTimeZoneInformation`](/docs/api/windows/time-zone#get-time-zone-information).

<h2 id="time-zone-rule-date"><code>TimeZoneRuleDate</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct TimeZoneRuleDate {
    pub year: uint16;
    pub month: uint16;
    pub dayOfWeek: uint16;
    pub day: uint16;
    pub hour: uint16;
    pub minute: uint16;
    pub second: uint16;
    pub milliseconds: uint16;
}
```

When a time-zone rule takes effect, in the layout of `SYSTEMTIME` but read as a rule, not a date.
A rule with `year` zero recurs every year: in `month`, on the `day`th occurrence of `dayOfWeek` (Sunday is zero),
where the fifth occurrence means the last, at `hour`:`minute` local time. A zero `month` means the zone has no
daylight time.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/timezoneapi/ns-timezoneapi-time_zone_information](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/timezoneapi/ns-timezoneapi-time_zone_information)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/TimeZone.rux#L9)

**Fields**

| Name           | Type     | Description                                                                  |
| -------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `year`         | `uint16` | The year for a one-time change, or zero for a rule that recurs.              |
| `month`        | `uint16` | The month, 1 through 12, or zero when there is no change.                    |
| `dayOfWeek`    | `uint16` | The day of the week, Sunday being zero.                                      |
| `day`          | `uint16` | Which occurrence of that day in the month, 1 through 5, where 5 is the last. |
| `hour`         | `uint16` | The hour of the change, in the local time before it.                         |
| `minute`       | `uint16` | The minute of the change.                                                    |
| `second`       | `uint16` | The second of the change.                                                    |
| `milliseconds` | `uint16` | The millisecond of the change.                                               |

<h2 id="time-zone-information"><code>TimeZoneInformation</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct TimeZoneInformation {
    pub bias: int32;
    pub standardName: uint16[N];
    pub standardDate: TimeZoneRuleDate;
    pub standardBias: int32;
    pub daylightName: uint16[N];
    pub daylightDate: TimeZoneRuleDate;
    pub daylightBias: int32;
}
```

Win32's `TIME_ZONE_INFORMATION`: a zone's offsets and when its daylight time starts and ends.
Each bias is minutes to add to local time to get UTC, so a zone east of Greenwich has a negative one.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/timezoneapi/ns-timezoneapi-time_zone_information](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/timezoneapi/ns-timezoneapi-time_zone_information)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/TimeZone.rux#L32)

**Fields**

| Name           | Type               | Description                                                 |
| -------------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bias`         | `int32`            | The bias of standard time, in minutes.                      |
| `standardName` | `uint16[N]`        | The name of standard time, NUL-terminated UTF-16.           |
| `standardDate` | `TimeZoneRuleDate` | When standard time starts.                                  |
| `standardBias` | `int32`            | What is added to `bias` during standard time, usually zero. |
| `daylightName` | `uint16[N]`        | The name of daylight time, NUL-terminated UTF-16.           |
| `daylightDate` | `TimeZoneRuleDate` | When daylight time starts.                                  |
| `daylightBias` | `int32`            | What is added to `bias` during daylight time, usually -60.  |

<h2 id="get-time-zone-information"><code>GetTimeZoneInformation</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func GetTimeZoneInformation(information: *var TimeZoneInformation) -> uint32
```

Reads the system's current time zone.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/timezoneapi/nf-timezoneapi-gettimezoneinformation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/timezoneapi/nf-timezoneapi-gettimezoneinformation)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/TimeZone.rux#L56)

**Parameters**

| Name          | Type                       | Description       |
| ------------- | -------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `information` | `*var TimeZoneInformation` | receives the zone |

**Returns**: which part of the year it is now, or `0xFFFFFFFF` on failure with the reason in [`GetLastError`](/docs/api/windows/errors#get-last-error)
